explication:
## Purpose and entry points
TinyCC is a compact ANSI C compiler, linker, and direct-execution runtime. It supports C compilation, `-run` scripting/JIT-style execution, object/executable/shared-library output, and embedding through libtcc. The CLI entry point is `tcc.c`; the public embedding API is `libtcc.h` with implementation in `libtcc.c`.

## Compiler state and command orchestration
`TCCState` and shared compiler definitions coordinate options, include/library paths, symbol tables, output mode, target selection, and diagnostics across all stages. The CLI parses arguments and drives compilation/link/run workflows; libtcc exposes the same core engine to host programs.
- `tcc.c`
- `tcc.h`
- `libtcc.c`
- `libtcc.h`

## Front end: preprocessing, tokens, parsing, semantics
The preprocessor resolves source files, headers, macros, conditional compilation, and tokenization. The C generator/parser consumes that token stream, builds type/symbol state, evaluates expressions, and emits target operations. This is the principal source-language boundary: C and assembly inputs become internal compiler/linker state.
- `tccpp.c`
- `tcctok.h`
- `tccgen.c`
- `tccasm.c`

## Target code generation and assemblers
Backend selection is compile-time/target-dependent. C code generation feeds architecture-specific instruction encoding and relocation generation for i386, x86-64, ARM, AArch64, RISC-V64, and C67. Each supported ISA has distinct codegen, assembler, and usually linker support, so target changes cross a substantial boundary rather than merely an output-format option.
- `i386-gen.c`
- `x86_64-gen.c`
- `arm64-gen.c`
- `riscv64-gen.c`

## Object formats, linking, and binary emission
The internal linker combines generated objects, libraries, symbols, relocations, and startup/runtime pieces. Format-specific modules read/write ELF, PE/COFF, and Mach-O artifacts; debug metadata support includes DWARF and stabs. Link mode determines whether results are persisted as files or prepared for in-memory execution.
- `tccelf.c`
- `tccpe.c`
- `tccmacho.c`
- `tcccoff.c`
- `elf.h`

## In-memory execution and safety instrumentation
`-run` and libtcc can relocate generated code into process memory and invoke its entry point rather than producing a standalone binary. Optional bounds checking instruments code and uses a runtime with logging, executable/DLL hooks, and signal-related support; checked and ordinary code can coexist.
- `tccrun.c`
- `lib/runmain.c`
- `lib/bcheck.c`
- `lib/bt-exe.c`

## Runtime, platform surface, and distribution
Compiler-generated programs depend on bundled support routines for compiler builtins, atomics, varargs, allocation, PIC, and architecture-specific ABI details. Bundled minimal headers provide a lightweight C environment; Windows additionally ships CRT startup sources, import definitions, and Win32-compatible headers. Hosts are Unix-like systems and Windows, built through `configure`/Make or Windows batch scripts; no networked service is required.
- `lib/libtcc1.c`
- `lib/builtin.c`
- `include/tccdefs.h`
- `win32/lib/crt1.c`
- `win32/build-tcc.bat`
